source_batch.unit_label: Module A unit 4: Correlation and Regression

facts.statement: Correlation studies whether two variables are related; regression estimates the value of one variable when the value of the other is given. The unit covers two variables only. A scatter diagram plots the data pairs (x, y): points rising from left to right show a direct relationship, points falling show an inverse relationship, and a shapeless cloud shows no relationship. A relationship that a straight line can fit is linear; one that needs a curve (for example inverse at first and direct later) is curvilinear. The closer the points lie to the fitted line, the stronger the relationship and the more accurate the predictions.

The correlation coefficient is r = cov(X, Y) / (sigma_x sigma_y), where cov(X, Y) = (1/N) Sum (x - x-bar)(y - y-bar) and sigma_x and sigma_y are the standard deviations (divisor N). The equivalent computing formula is r = (N Sum xy - Sum x Sum y) / ( sqrt(N Sum x^2 - (Sum x)^2) x sqrt(N Sum y^2 - (Sum y)^2) ).

The value of r always lies between -1 and +1. r = -1 is a perfect inverse relationship (all points on a line of negative slope), r = +1 a perfect direct relationship (all points on a line of positive slope), and r = 0 means no linear relationship (a curvilinear relationship may still exist). A value near +1 or -1 indicates a strong relationship and a value near zero a weak one.

The courseware computes r = 0.8383 for seven pairs of exports of raw materials (42, 44, 58, 55, 89, 98, 66) and imports of finished goods (56, 59, 53, 58, 65, 78, 58), with Sum x = 452, Sum y = 427, Sum x^2 printed as 31,940 (the seven squares in its own table add to 31,970), Sum y^2 = 26,463 and Sum xy = 28,469; the printed totals give r = 0.8383, whereas the corrected total gives r = 0.8336. For a second case with Sum (x - x-bar)(y - y-bar) = 740, variances 204 and 506 and 20 observations, a covariance of 37 and r = 0.115.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 76-78, Examples 4.1 and 4.2 (Sum x^2 total in the courseware is mis-added)

facts.statement: Regression fits the line y = a + bx by the method of least squares so that the line passes close to all points with points on both sides. The slope is b = cov(X, Y) / sigma_x^2 (equivalently ((1/N) Sum xy - x-bar y-bar) / ((1/N) Sum x^2 - x-bar^2)) and the intercept is a = y-bar - b x-bar. A positive b slopes upward from left to right and a negative b downward. The predicted value of y for a given x is y-hat = a + bx. In the courseware example the printed line is y = 39.96 + 0.3258x, giving y-hat = 62.77 for x = 70 (with the corrected Sum x^2 the line is y = 40.19 + 0.3222x and y-hat = 62.75).

The standard error of the estimate is Se = sqrt( Sum (y - y-hat)^2 / (n - 2) ), which can also be written sqrt( (Sum y^2 - a Sum y - b Sum xy) / (n - 2) ). A small Se means the estimates are fairly accurate. The courseware says the actual y lies between y-hat - Se and y-hat + Se with 65 per cent confidence, and between y-hat - 2 Se and y-hat + 2 Se with 95 per cent confidence. In its example Se = 5 (5.04 with the corrected total) for x = 70, so the actual y is expected between about 57.77 and 67.77 (and between 52.77 and 72.77 at 95 per cent).

The correlation coefficient measures only linear relationships: a perfect curvilinear relationship such as points on a circle gives r near zero. The data should be homogeneous, since a heterogeneous sample can give a high r where no real correlation exists (spurious correlation). A value of r near 1 shows that the variables rise and fall together, not that one causes the other: annual rice consumption and road accidents in India both rose over 20 years, but neither causes the other.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 81-82, Limitation of the Coefficient of Correlation

facts.statement: The independent variable is the variable that is the basis of prediction, and the dependent variable is the variable that is predicted. Regression analysis is the fitting of the line of relationship.

payload.title: Scatter diagrams: seeing a relationship before measuring it
payload.core_explanation_md:
Before any formula, **plot the pairs**. Put one variable on the horizontal axis (the one you use for prediction, the **independent** variable) and the other on the vertical axis (the **dependent** variable, the one you want to predict). Each customer, branch or month becomes one dot.

| Pattern of dots | Relationship |
| --- | --- |
| Rise from left to right | Direct (positive) |
| Fall from left to right | Inverse (negative) |
| Shapeless cloud | None |
| Falls then rises, or bends | Curvilinear |

If a straight line can run through the dots, the relationship is **linear**. The tighter the dots hug the line, the stronger the relationship and the better the predictions. This unit deals only with linear relationships.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Two scatter diagrams can both show a direct relationship yet differ in strength. A diagram only gives a rough feel; correlation puts a number on the strength and regression gives the line for predicting.

self_check.prompt_text: Branch advertising spend is plotted against new accounts opened. Which variable would you put on the horizontal axis if you want to predict accounts from spend?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Advertising spend: it is the independent variable, the basis of the prediction.

payload.title: Correlation coefficient r
payload.core_explanation_md:
The correlation coefficient asks: when x is above its average, is y usually above its average too? Multiply each pair of deviations, average the products (the **covariance**), then divide by the two standard deviations so that the answer has no units.

For hand calculation use the sums version. Tabulate x, y, x squared, y squared and xy, total each column, and substitute. It avoids computing every deviation.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Dividing by the standard deviations is what keeps r between -1 and +1 and makes it comparable across problems: rupees against months gives the same kind of number as kilograms against metres.

formula_spec.latex_expression: r = \frac{\operatorname{cov}(X,Y)}{\sigma_x\sigma_y} = \frac{N\sum xy - \sum x \sum y}{\sqrt{N\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2}\,\sqrt{N\sum y^2 - (\sum y)^2}}

variables.name: Standard deviations of x and y (divisor N)

assumptions: The same N pairs are used in every sum.
Standard deviations use divisor N, matching the covariance.
common_errors: Mixing divisors (N for covariance, N - 1 for a standard deviation).
Confusing the sum of squares with the square of the sum.
Reporting r outside the range -1 to +1 (a sign that an arithmetic slip occurred).

self_check.prompt_text: cov(X, Y) = 12, sigma_x = 3, sigma_y = 5. What is r?

payload.title: Reading the value of r
payload.core_explanation_md:
r is a **dial** from -1 to +1.

| r | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| +1 | Perfect direct linear relationship: all points on an upward line |
| Near +1 | Strong direct relationship |
| Near 0 | Weak or no *linear* relationship |
| Near -1 | Strong inverse relationship |
| -1 | Perfect inverse linear relationship: all points on a downward line |

Two habits keep you honest. First, the **sign** gives direction and the **size** gives strength, so -0.9 is stronger than +0.5. Second, r = 0 says there is no *linear* relationship, not that the variables are unrelated: a curved pattern can have r close to 0.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: A computed |r| above 1 is always an arithmetic mistake. Check your sums.

self_check.prompt_text: Which shows the stronger relationship: r = -0.85 or r = +0.60?
self_check.expected_takeaway: r = -0.85: strength is the size of r, and the sign only shows the direction (here inverse).

payload.title: The least-squares regression line
payload.core_explanation_md:
Regression draws the one straight line that fits the dots best in the **least squares** sense: it makes the total of the squared vertical gaps between the dots and the line as small as possible.

The line is y-hat = a + bx.

- The **slope** b says how much y changes, on average, for one unit increase in x. Positive slopes rise, negative slopes fall.
- The **intercept** a is where the line cuts the y-axis. Because the line passes through the point of averages, a = y-bar minus b times x-bar.

To predict, put the given x into the equation.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Notice that b is a covariance divided by the *variance of x*, not by a standard deviation: it carries the units of y per unit of x, so it has units, unlike r.

variables.name: Slope of the line
variables.unit: units of y per unit of x

assumptions: x is the independent variable and y the dependent variable; the line predicts y from x.
common_errors: Dividing the covariance by sigma_x instead of its square.
Computing a with the wrong sign.
Using the line to predict x from y.

self_check.prompt_text: x-bar = 20, y-bar = 70 and b = 2. What is a, and what does the line predict for x = 25?

payload.title: Standard error of the estimate: how good is the prediction?
payload.core_explanation_md:
A regression line always gives *a* prediction, but how reliable is it? Measure the gaps between actual y and the line's y-hat. Square them, add, divide by **n - 2** (two quantities, a and b, were estimated from the data) and take the root.

A **small** Se means the dots hug the line and predictions are accurate. As a working rule from the courseware, the actual value is expected within about one Se either side of the prediction roughly two-thirds of the time, and within two Se about 95 per cent of the time.

If you have already found a and b, the sums form saves finding every y-hat.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Se is in the units of y, so judge it against the size of the y values: an Se of 5 matters less when y is around 60 than when it is around 10.

formula_spec.latex_expression: S_e = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (y-\hat{y})^2}{n-2}} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum y^2 - a\sum y - b\sum xy}{n-2}}
assumptions: The line has been fitted by least squares to the same data.
common_errors: Dividing by n or n - 1 instead of n - 2.
Using y-bar in place of y-hat.
Forgetting that Se has the units of y.

self_check.prompt_text: Sum of squared residuals is 36 and n = 11. What is Se, and what band does two Se give around a prediction of 50?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Se = sqrt(36 / 9) = 2; the band is 50 plus or minus 4, that is 46 to 54 (about 95 per cent).

payload.title: Limits of correlation: line only, careful data, no causation
payload.core_explanation_md:
A high r is not the end of the analysis. Three cautions:

- **Linear only.** r measures straight-line association. Points laid out on a perfect circle have r near zero even though the pattern is exact.
- **Homogeneous data.** If you mix two different groups in one sample, r can look high when there is no real relationship inside either group. That is **spurious correlation**.
- **Not causation.** r near 1 shows that two variables rise and fall together. It does not show that one causes the other: annual rice consumption and road accidents both climbed together over twenty years, yet neither drives the other.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Before acting on a correlation, ask what else could drive both variables, and look at the scatter diagram, not only the number.

self_check.prompt_text: Deposits and the number of ATMs in a town both rise for ten years and r = 0.95. Can you conclude that more ATMs cause more deposits?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. A high r shows they move together, not that one causes the other; growth in the town's economy could drive both.

payload.title: Advertising spend and new accounts: r, the regression line and Se
payload.core_explanation_md: Five branches spent x = 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 (Rs lakh) on advertising and opened y = 3, 5, 6, 9 and 12 (hundreds of) new accounts. Find r, the regression line of y on x, the predicted accounts for x = 7, and the standard error of the estimate.

worked_steps.formula_or_substitution: Sum x, Sum y, Sum xy, Sum x^2, Sum y^2

worked_steps.description: Sum of squared residuals by the sums form.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: r = 0.9839 (very strong direct relationship); y-hat = 0.4 + 1.1x; for Rs 7 lakh of advertising about 810 new accounts, give or take about 73 (one Se)

self_check.prompt_text: What does the slope 1.1 mean in plain words?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Each extra Rs 1 lakh of advertising goes with about 110 more new accounts (1.1 hundred), on average.

payload.title: From covariance and variances to r and the slope
payload.core_explanation_md: For 20 pairs of observations Sum (x - x-bar)(y - y-bar) = 360, the variance of x is 100 and the variance of y is 225 (divisor N). Find the covariance, r, and the slope of the regression of y on x.
payload.final_answer_with_unit: Covariance 18; r = 0.12 (very weak direct linear relationship); slope b = 0.18

self_check.prompt_text: The slope is 0.18. Does a small slope by itself mean the relationship is weak?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The slope depends on the units of x and y; the unit-free measure of strength is r, which here (0.12) does show a very weak linear relationship.

payload.stem_md: A scatter diagram of loan-to-deposit ratio (x) and net interest margin (y) across branches shows points that fall steadily from top left to bottom right. The relationship is

options.text_md: Direct, because both variables are measured for the same branches
options.explanation_md: Direct means y rises as x rises; here y falls.

options.text_md: Inverse, because y tends to fall as x rises
options.explanation_md: Points falling from left to right show an inverse relationship.

options.text_md: Absent, because the points do not form a perfect line
options.explanation_md: A pattern need not be perfect to indicate a relationship.

options.text_md: Curvilinear, because the points fall
options.explanation_md: A steady fall that a straight line fits is linear.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Falling points from left to right indicate an inverse (negative) linear relationship.

payload.stem_md: The points on a scatter diagram fall at first and then rise, forming a U shape. Which statement is best?

options.text_md: The relationship is perfectly linear
options.explanation_md: A U shape cannot be fitted by one straight line.

options.text_md: The relationship is direct throughout
options.explanation_md: It is inverse at first.

options.text_md: The relationship is curvilinear, so a straight-line correlation measure would understate it
options.explanation_md: A relationship that needs a curve is curvilinear, and r measures only linear association.

options.text_md: The variables must be independent of each other
options.explanation_md: A clear pattern shows a relationship, just not a linear one.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A U-shaped pattern is curvilinear; r, which measures linear association, can be near zero even though the relationship is strong.

payload.stem_md: Which of these cannot be a correlation coefficient?

options.explanation_md: Within the range -1 to +1.
Zero is allowed and means no linear relationship.
Perfect direct linear relationship.
r always lies between -1 and +1, so 1.25 signals an arithmetic error.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The correlation coefficient always lies between -1 and +1.

payload.stem_md: For two sets of branches, r = -0.90 for pair A and r = +0.60 for pair B. Which statement is correct?

options.text_md: Pair A has a stronger relationship, and it is inverse
options.explanation_md: Strength is the size of r: 0.90 is greater than 0.60, and the negative sign shows an inverse relationship.

options.text_md: Pair B is more strongly related because its r is positive
options.explanation_md: The sign gives direction only.

options.text_md: Pair A has no relationship because r is negative
options.explanation_md: A negative r is a relationship in the inverse direction.

options.text_md: The two are equally strong
options.explanation_md: 0.90 is larger than 0.60.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The size of r shows strength; the sign shows direction. -0.90 is stronger than +0.60 and is inverse.

payload.stem_md: Variables x and y lie exactly on a circle and r is computed as nearly 0. What should be concluded?

options.text_md: There is no relationship between x and y
options.explanation_md: The relationship is exact, only not linear.

options.text_md: There is no linear relationship, but a curvilinear relationship may exist
options.explanation_md: r = 0 means no linear relationship; other relationships may exist.

options.text_md: The data are spurious
options.explanation_md: Spurious correlation concerns a falsely high r from mixed data.

options.text_md: The calculation must be wrong, since exact patterns give r = 1
options.explanation_md: Only exact straight-line patterns give r = 1.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The correlation coefficient measures only linear association, so an exact circular pattern gives r near zero.

payload.stem_md: In the line y-hat = a + bx, a negative slope b means

options.text_md: y tends to rise as x rises
options.explanation_md: That is a positive slope.

options.text_md: The intercept is negative
options.explanation_md: The sign of b does not decide the sign of a.

options.text_md: y tends to fall as x rises
options.explanation_md: A negative slope runs downward from left to right.

options.text_md: r must equal -1
options.explanation_md: A negative slope only means a negative r, not a perfect one.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A negative slope means the line falls from left to right: y tends to fall as x rises.

payload.stem_md: The least-squares line y-hat = a + bx always passes through the point

options.explanation_md: It cuts the y-axis at a, which need not be zero.

options.text_md: The first data point
options.explanation_md: No data point need lie on the line.

options.text_md: The point of the two medians
options.explanation_md: The line is built from means, not medians.

options.text_md: (x-bar, y-bar), the point of the two means
options.explanation_md: Since a = y-bar - b x-bar, substituting x = x-bar gives y-hat = y-bar.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The intercept formula a = y-bar - b x-bar means the line passes through (x-bar, y-bar).

payload.stem_md: Two regression lines are fitted to different data sets with the same y units. Line 1 has Se = 2 and line 2 has Se = 9. Which statement is right?

options.text_md: Line 1 gives the more accurate predictions
options.explanation_md: A smaller standard error of estimate means the points lie closer to the line.

options.text_md: Line 2 gives the more accurate predictions
options.explanation_md: Its Se is larger, so the points scatter more.

options.text_md: They are equally accurate
options.explanation_md: The Se values differ.

options.text_md: Se says nothing about accuracy
options.explanation_md: It measures how well the line predicts.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A small standard error of the estimate indicates that estimates are fairly accurate.

payload.stem_md: A survey pools two very different groups of customers and finds a high correlation between two variables, though within each group there is none. This is an example of

options.text_md: Perfect correlation
options.explanation_md: r is not 1 here and the issue is how the data were drawn.

options.text_md: Spurious correlation, caused by non-homogeneous data
options.explanation_md: A heterogeneous sample can give a high r although no correlation actually exists.

options.text_md: Curvilinear correlation
options.explanation_md: The problem is mixing groups, not curvature.

options.text_md: Inverse correlation
options.explanation_md: Inverse refers to direction, not to the problem.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A non-homogeneous sample can show a high correlation where none really exists: spurious correlation.

payload.stem_md: Household income and credit card spending in a city have a correlation coefficient of 0.92. What may be concluded?

options.text_md: Higher income causes higher spending
options.explanation_md: Correlation alone does not establish cause and effect.

options.text_md: Spending causes income
options.explanation_md: Cause and effect cannot be established from r.

options.text_md: The two tend to rise and fall together, but r alone does not show cause and effect
options.explanation_md: A high r shows association, not causation.

options.text_md: They are unrelated
options.explanation_md: An r of 0.92 shows strong association.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A value of r close to 1 shows the variables move together; it does not indicate a cause-and-effect relationship.

payload.stem_md: A bank wants to predict monthly deposits from the number of active customers. The independent variable is

options.text_md: Monthly deposits, because it is what the bank cares about
options.explanation_md: That is the dependent variable, the one predicted.

options.text_md: Neither, because both are measured together
options.explanation_md: One is the basis, the other is predicted.

options.text_md: The regression line itself
options.explanation_md: The line is the fitted relationship, not a variable.

options.text_md: The number of active customers, the basis of the prediction
options.explanation_md: The independent variable is the one used to predict.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The independent variable is the basis of prediction; the dependent variable is the one predicted.

items.title: Standard error of the estimate: how good is the prediction?
items.core_explanation_md:
A regression line always gives *a* prediction, but how reliable is it? Measure the gaps between actual y and the line's y-hat. Square them, add, divide by **n - 2** (two quantities, a and b, were estimated from the data) and take the root.

A **small** Se means the dots hug the line and predictions are accurate. As a working rule from the courseware, the actual value is expected within about one Se either side of the prediction roughly two-thirds of the time, and within two Se about 95 per cent of the time.

If you have already found a and b, the sums form saves finding every y-hat.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Se is in the units of y, so judge it against the size of the y values: an Se of 5 matters less when y is around 60 than when it is around 10.

formula_spec.latex_expression: S_e = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (y-\hat{y})^2}{n-2}} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum y^2 - a\sum y - b\sum xy}{n-2}}
assumptions: The line has been fitted by least squares to the same data.
common_errors: Dividing by n or n - 1 instead of n - 2.
Using y-bar in place of y-hat.
Forgetting that Se has the units of y.

self_check.prompt_text: Sum of squared residuals is 36 and n = 11. What is Se, and what band does two Se give around a prediction of 50?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Se = sqrt(36 / 9) = 2; the band is 50 plus or minus 4, that is 46 to 54 (about 95 per cent).

items.title: Limits of correlation: line only, careful data, no causation
items.core_explanation_md:
A high r is not the end of the analysis. Three cautions:

- **Linear only.** r measures straight-line association. Points laid out on a perfect circle have r near zero even though the pattern is exact.
- **Homogeneous data.** If you mix two different groups in one sample, r can look high when there is no real relationship inside either group. That is **spurious correlation**.
- **Not causation.** r near 1 shows that two variables rise and fall together. It does not show that one causes the other: annual rice consumption and road accidents both climbed together over twenty years, yet neither drives the other.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Before acting on a correlation, ask what else could drive both variables, and look at the scatter diagram, not only the number.

self_check.prompt_text: Deposits and the number of ATMs in a town both rise for ten years and r = 0.95. Can you conclude that more ATMs cause more deposits?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. A high r shows they move together, not that one causes the other; growth in the town's economy could drive both.

items.title: Advertising spend and new accounts: r, the regression line and Se
items.core_explanation_md: Five branches spent x = 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 (Rs lakh) on advertising and opened y = 3, 5, 6, 9 and 12 (hundreds of) new accounts. Find r, the regression line of y on x, the predicted accounts for x = 7, and the standard error of the estimate.

worked_steps.formula_or_substitution: Sum x, Sum y, Sum xy, Sum x^2, Sum y^2

worked_steps.description: Sum of squared residuals by the sums form.

items.final_answer_with_unit: r = 0.9839 (very strong direct relationship); y-hat = 0.4 + 1.1x; for Rs 7 lakh of advertising about 810 new accounts, give or take about 73 (one Se)

self_check.prompt_text: What does the slope 1.1 mean in plain words?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Each extra Rs 1 lakh of advertising goes with about 110 more new accounts (1.1 hundred), on average.

items.title: From covariance and variances to r and the slope
items.core_explanation_md: For 20 pairs of observations Sum (x - x-bar)(y - y-bar) = 360, the variance of x is 100 and the variance of y is 225 (divisor N). Find the covariance, r, and the slope of the regression of y on x.
items.final_answer_with_unit: Covariance 18; r = 0.12 (very weak direct linear relationship); slope b = 0.18

self_check.prompt_text: The slope is 0.18. Does a small slope by itself mean the relationship is weak?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The slope depends on the units of x and y; the unit-free measure of strength is r, which here (0.12) does show a very weak linear relationship.

items.stem_md: A scatter diagram of loan-to-deposit ratio (x) and net interest margin (y) across branches shows points that fall steadily from top left to bottom right. The relationship is

options.text_md: Direct, because both variables are measured for the same branches
options.explanation_md: Direct means y rises as x rises; here y falls.

options.text_md: Inverse, because y tends to fall as x rises
options.explanation_md: Points falling from left to right show an inverse relationship.

options.text_md: Absent, because the points do not form a perfect line
options.explanation_md: A pattern need not be perfect to indicate a relationship.

options.text_md: Curvilinear, because the points fall
options.explanation_md: A steady fall that a straight line fits is linear.

items.correct_explanation_md: Falling points from left to right indicate an inverse (negative) linear relationship.

options.text_md: Spurious correlation, caused by non-homogeneous data
options.explanation_md: A heterogeneous sample can give a high r although no correlation actually exists.

options.text_md: Curvilinear correlation
options.explanation_md: The problem is mixing groups, not curvature.

options.text_md: Inverse correlation
options.explanation_md: Inverse refers to direction, not to the problem.
